holes_found.description: "The SAME code and words as for the dome card" (DR:registered_prediction_scorecard.B1-M-001.as_if_DR1) is not quite true. In rev5_dr1_unified.py the card branch labels FALSIFIED as-if only when 3-sigma injection power >= 0.8 at the claimed value in every admitted variant (testable_all_variants), and it counts any surviving detection within CARD_BAND + 2 null SD as consistent with the card. The B1-M-001 branch labels FALSIFIED as-if whenever any variant's 3-sigma threshold lies above -25 nT. It has no power gate and no +2 SD margin. The rule text states the power gate as part of DR-1 (DR:symmetric_evaluation_rules.DR-1_detectability_override.rev5_unified_standard: "rev5 also requires 3-sigma injection power >= 0.8 at the claimed value"). Effect: at ESK the power at -25 nT, the band's most testable point, is 0.56-0.84 (7 of 8 variants below 0.8). At LER it is 0.32-0.76 (all 8 below 0.8, including the quadratic variants the draft relies on: 0.72/0.76/0.68/0.44). Under the stated gate the ESK and LER "sliver" is UNTESTED, not "absent". So SC-26, which overturned rev4's "untested" at those stations, is itself wrong under rev5's own rule. At the other five stations the quoted "upper portion" boundaries are the 3-sigma thresholds. Amplitudes just beyond a threshold have only about 50% power, so under the 0.8 gate the falsified portion starts about 0.84 SD further out (e.g. HAD power at -17.8 nT is 0.60-0.84). Direction: this asymmetry is harsher on our own band. No dome label changes, because card power is 0.95-1.00 in every admitted cell. But the file's central claim, "one code, identical words", is checkably false, and it mislabels two of our stations.
holes_found.recommendation: Make the two branches identical, choosing either option and saying which. (i) Recommended: apply the power gate to both. For our band, compute the 0.8-power amplitude per station and variant by injection (the same devs loop at a grid of amplitudes). Report the falsified portion as [-25, a80], label ESK and LER UNTESTED (retract SC-26; rev4 was right), and use the same consistency margin on both sides (either +2 SD for both, or none for both). (ii) Alternatively, drop the power gate from the card branch and from the rule text, so DR-1 is threshold-only as originally defined (2026-09-27). SC-26 then stands, and the card label is unchanged. Under either option, re-run, update the B1-M-001 as_if_DR1 text, SC-26 and the rev5_change_log line, and keep "SAME code" only if it is literally true. Outcome for the dome: unchanged either way.

holes_found.description: A dome-favourable result is missing, and a "no outcome changes" statement is false. DR:prediction_level.PRED_095.registrations.card.arithmetic_note says "on the formula value -17.43 +/- 2 every result below is unchanged", and DII-1 says "No scoring outcome changes". But the frozen-protocol peak R2 at SPT is -15.60 nT (DR:prediction_level.PRED_095.card_scored_on_registered_component_H.readings.R2_frozen_protocol_peak). That is outside the stated claim band [-19.8, -15.8] by 0.20 nT, and INSIDE the card's own formula-value band [-19.43, -15.43]. Reproduced this run (independent R2 script on the rev4 inputs: SPT -15.60, EBR -13.69). Context that weakens it: R2 is a +/-60 min peak, not "during totality"; it is not a DR-1 quantity; and 3 of 25 SPT control days also fall in that band, so it is non-diagnostic. It still has to be disclosed, because it is exactly the kind of result the erratum symmetry obligation exists for. The c4 review made the same unchecked claim in its C4-5 recommendation ("the band shift does not change any outcome"); that was our error too.
holes_found.recommendation: Change the arithmetic_note and DII-1 to say: "On the formula value -17.43 +/- 2 the DR-1 results are unchanged; one non-DR-1 completeness reading changes: SPT's frozen-protocol peak (-15.60 nT) falls inside the formula-value claim band (it is 0.20 nT outside the stated band); 3 of 25 SPT control days do the same, and R2 is a +/-60 min peak, not a during-totality reading." Add a dome_favourable_findings line with the same caveats. Add a self_correction noting that rev5 and c4 both said "no outcome changes".

holes_found.description: The definitive-data re-run rule (DR:stamp_preconditions.definitive_data_rerun_rule) is close, but not yet mechanical. HNOTE asks "what counts as material; which labels can flip". (a) "A label changes (falsified / untested / pending, per registration)" has no fixed list of registrations and no field paths. Under Option B every label is "pending" whatever the data say, so the test is vacuous unless it compares the DR-1 as-if labels. (b) "A stated SD distance crosses 3" does not say which distances. The file states dozens, and the -10.9 linear range (1.49-3.18) already straddles 3. The power gate (0.8) and the CTL-1 discount set can also flip a label, and the rule does not name them. (c) "Re-run every script ... unchanged" does not say that the input request changes to publicationState=definitive and that the manifest is regenerated. (d) No trigger or deadline is set if definitive data arrive for some stations and not others, or never. (e) It does not say whether an addendum with no material change still publishes the new numbers.
holes_found.recommendation: Add to the stamped file an explicit label_table: registration -> as-if label -> output JSON path (e.g. rev5_dr1_unified.json:card_PRED_095.EBR.admissible_verdict.label; ours_B1_M_001_upper_portion.<st>.upper_portion_label; lag-joint summary keys; contact-phase power rows), with today's values. Add a numbers_to_compare list (the headline-quoted figures). Declare material = any label in the table changes, OR any listed number crosses 3 (SD) or 0.8 (power), OR the CTL-1 discount set changes. State that the only change allowed is publicationState=definitive, with a regenerated manifest. Set the trigger as: when definitive data exist for EBR, SPT, the 8 Z-joint stations and ASC/KOU/HER, or on a fixed date (e.g. 2027-12-31) with whatever is available, gaps listed. Always publish the full re-run outputs and diff, even when the result is "no material change".

decision_6: recommend (b) now, with (a) as an upgrade. Stamp over a private archive whose sha256 is in the stamped file, so the stamp does not wait on a third party. At the same time, ask the INTERMAGNET Secretary and the operating institutes whether a ~13 MB research archive counts as "bulk distribution". If permission comes, publish it under predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-results-inputs/ with the CC BY-NC notice and the acknowledgement text, and record that in a separately stamped addendum. Reject (c). Other side, considered: (a) alone gives the strongest public verifiability, and CC BY-NC allows non-commercial redistribution. But the INTERMAGNET page adds a separate permission clause for "bulk distribution to third parties", and 809 files from 12 observatories under several institutes could be read as bulk. The ask is cheap; an unasked public dump is the only option with a downside we cannot undo. (Not legal advice.)

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome's eclipse registrations contain real, checkable content, and rev5 credits it. The card's own falsifier (H within +/-3 nT of 0 during totality) did not fire on the raw reading, EBR -9.61 / SPT -12.56 nT (DR:prediction_level.PRED_095.card_scored_on_registered_component_H.readings.R1_raw_deviation_at_maximum), reproduced this run. SPT's frozen-protocol peak (-15.60 nT) even sits inside the card's own formula-value band (C5-2, reproduced this run). The dome's timing words ("within 30 minutes", "umbra-locked", "during totality"; monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:73, :108, :1426) are specific enough to bound the admissible lag. That is what lets rev5 test the x1.672 amplitude without choosing a lag after seeing the data.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: At the lags the card's own text admits, -17.8 nT was testable (power 1.00) and is 4.1-7.7 SD from every eclipse-attributable fit, with no detection at all (rev5_dr1_unified.json:card_PRED_095.EBR.admissible_tau0_15; reproduced independently this run). The R2 overlap is a +/-60 min peak, not a during-totality reading, and 3 of 25 ordinary SPT days do the same. The paragraph's x1.672 Z amplitude is rejected at >= 3.72 control SD for lag-matched templates within the dome's own 30-minute bound (DR:z_component_evaluation.power_at_dome_formula_amplitudes.joint_amplitude_test.result_x1672). And the dome's own Kp and BOU preconditions void the test formally, which the file states first (DR:headline).

deeper_analysis: Which way does each residual cut? C5-1 is harsher on us: it labels two of our stations falsified where the stated rule says untested. C5-2 hides a weak dome-favourable reading. C5-4/C5-5 make our case read slightly stronger than the numbers. None changes a dome label. That pattern, small errors that mostly flatter our side's presentation, is the reason the frozen-prediction rule says to attack our side too. With them fixed, the file's claims match its code exactly, and that is the property a stamped results file needs. I looked for a reason to escalate to deep-attack and found none.
